newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on local and fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on local and fund selling.

text.p: Late local and fund selling drove CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
"It was a hatchet job with people just getting cut up today," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "The wheat will get planted, it will get in the ground."

Wheat was firm in early dealings on mounting talk that U.S. soft red winter wheat acreage for 1997 may be trimmed by the late harvest of the U.S. soybean crop. A fair portion of the soft red winter wheat acreage is planted after the soy crop has been combined.
After the close, USDA said the overall U.S. soybean harvest was 40 percent complete as of Sunday, behind the 52 percent average.

Early support in futures came from an increase in daily exports. But USDA Tuesday released its weekly export inspections report during the session which cast a somewhat bearish pall on the wheat market.
USDA said for the week ended October 1, wheat inspections totaled 18.668 million bushels, well below trade expectations for 26 million to 28 million bushels.
Wheat futures closed 1-3/4 to 7-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 7-3/4 at $4.21-3/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000, up from 12,287 Monday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000, down from 3,728 Monday.
